title: Per-Process Heap vs Thread Stack Memory Model
prompt: Why isn't the heap 'one heap for the whole computer'? Explain what actually gets shared between threads.

forbidden_misconceptions: one heap for the entire computer
evaluator_rubric.scoring_criteria: Learner must explain that virtual memory gives each process an isolated address space and heap. Threads within a single process share the heap, data, and code segments, but each thread has its own private execution stack and registers.
evaluator_rubric.ideal_response_summary: Virtual memory provides each process with its own private virtual address space and heap. Independent processes cannot directly access each other's heaps without IPC. Threads within the same process share that process's heap and global memory, but each thread keeps its own isolated stack and CPU registers.
